newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish c.bank will not hold T-bills by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Polish c.bank will not hold T-bills by year-end.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland will not have any Polish treasury-bills in its portfolio by the end of this year, a finance ministry official said on Wednesday.
"All 436 million zlotys of T-bills which the NBP presently holds will mature before the end of the year," the director of the public debt department, Piotr Dziewulski, told Reuters.
He said the treasury aims in future only to finance the budget deficit through the central bank as a last resort and that it would not use debt instruments which mature past 1997. @

Earlier on Wednesday deputy finance minister Krzysztof Kalicki confirmed the treasury's aim to increase public debt financing by the non-banking sector, a move which will cut the inflationary growth of money supply.
"The finanace ministry would like to increase part of the public debt financed outside the banking system from the present 7.7 percent," Kalicki told a news conference.
He said that in developed countries about 10 percent of public debt is financed outside the banking sector. @

As of August 31 Poland had a total debt of 174 billion zlotys, including 107 billion foreign entitlement, compared to a 161 billion zloty debt at the end of 1995, with 101 billion worth of foreign debt.
